transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for gathering. As we head into the Friday press screening of Under Neon at the Calder Cinema, I need to finalize the public-screening protocol. The current draft has the full interview segment and a conventional open-floor audience Q&A. Before I approve anything, I want to check in with our clearance counsel and the event producer — are either of you on this call? I need to confirm there aren't any legal or event-format requirements I should be aware of before I sign off.

transcript.text: Mara, I need to flag a legal requirement before you approve anything. I reviewed a signed amendment that arrived this morning, and it confirms that the interview subject permits public screening only with the subject's face blurred and name omitted. I have not yet added the amendment to the master clearance memo, but the requirement is in effect.

Nina, the cinema's inability to support an open-floor microphone means the conventional Q&A format won't work either. Given both of these requirements are in effect, I cannot approve the current draft as-is. Here's what I'm prepared to do: I'll approve the protocol conditional on two changes — first, the interview segment must be modified to blur the subject's face and omit their name per the signed amendment; second, the audience Q&A must be switched to a card-based, moderator-read format per the venue's technical constraints. Elias, please get that amendment added to the master clearance memo. Nina, please update the event brief to reflect the card-based Q&A.
